content.text:
I reviewed each answer-key item against the record, checking figures against the meeting's final (corrected) numbers — notably the $132,000 W-2 correction (not $150,000), the $33,000 employer piece (not $37,500), the $57,500 2026 total (not $62,000), the $200,000 cash move (not $250,000), and the pension date moved from the 25th to October 9.

**Pairings:** all 13 key items are captured. Life events e1/e2/e3 → records 1/2/4. Account actions a1/a2/a3 → records 7/12/10 (records 8, 9 and 11 are splits of a1 and a2). Action items i1–i7 → records 13/16/17/18/19/14/15, with owners and dates matching the final versions (including the Jonas item reassigned to Marisol, and the LOC review tied to the October 1 quote return).

**Not-actions:** none of the four deferred/declined ideas (SEP rollover, cash balance plan, BOE disability policy, T-bill ladder) appear as actions — the record correctly omits them.

**Unpaired records:** 3, 5 and 6 are supported background facts (corrected salary detail, business cash and FDIC exposure, the undrawn line of credit). Records 8, 9 and 11 are duplicates that split the funding of the solo 401(k) and the brokerage account opening out of the umbrella items.

key_items.note: Brantmoor patient tower contract: 3 years, ~$1.2M total, milestone billing, first milestone ~$180,000 in November. All figures match the transcript.
First full-time W-2 project engineer in February 2027 at $95,000-$100,000. Added detail that the two contractors remain contractors is supported at [00:03:38].
Owen a senior, two early action applications due November 1, starting college next year (fall 2027). The added 529 balance of ~$96,000 matches [00:26:37].

Umbrella solo 401(k) item at Pellrose sponsored by the corporation with the corrected $57,500 2026 total (not the superseded $62,000). Growth 80/20 investment note is supported at [00:57:50]. Records 8 and 9 split out the deferral and profit-sharing components.

Moves the corrected $200,000 (not the initially proposed $250,000) to a government money market fund, authorized via the brokerage application funding section. Residual $210,000 operating / $248,000 at Marrowgate matches [00:17:46].
SEP discontinued with no 2026 contribution, account stays open, discontinuance letter to Pellrose plus participant notice. The $30,000 March funding correctly attributed to 2025.

Full e-signature package including adoption agreement, Pellrose plan application, deferral election, SEP discontinuance letter and notice, and brokerage application with corporate resolution. Devin Oakes, Tuesday the 22nd.
Key-person quotes at $1M and $1.5M, 10- and 15-year level term, company-owned and company-beneficiary, with the 101(j) notice-and-consent in the packet. Devin Oakes, Thursday October 1.
Corrected $132,000 salary and $33,000 employer contribution, deferral to start with the October 30 payroll. Correctly reassigned from Anneliese to Marisol at [00:25:21], due her October 6 meeting.
Pension estimate at age 61 via the member portal, sent to Anneliese. Graham Tendry, October 9 - the revised date, not the original Friday the 25th.
Projection rerun with Marisol at 58, Graham at 61 and the corrected $57,500 for 2026. Anneliese Corvath, before the December 8 meeting.
Marisol sends the Marrowgate line of credit agreement to Devin Oakes, Monday the 21st. Owner and date match [00:21:10]-[00:21:16].
Devin reviews the LOC agreement for life insurance, collateral assignment or covenant language before the quotes return, correctly tied to the October 1 quote date.

extra_items.note: Corrected 2026 W-2 of $132,000, $11,000/month, $88,000 YTD through August, and Jonas Peltier wanting $150,000 for 2027 reasonable compensation - all stated at [00:19:07]-[00:19:31]. Correctly records $150,000 as a 2027 target rather than the 2026 salary.
Undrawn $250,000 Marrowgate line of credit renewed in March with Marisol's personal guarantee, per [00:20:35]-[00:20:49].

Splits the $24,500 employee deferral component out of the solo 401(k) funding captured in record 7. Figures ($24,500, October 30 start, roughly 8/8/8.5) are accurate but it is a component of the same account action.
Splits the $33,000 employer profit-sharing component out of record 7. Correctly uses 25% of the corrected $132,000 and the pre-March-filing funding window, but duplicates the same account action.
Splits the opening of the corporate brokerage account at Pellrose out of the cash-move action in record 12, which already covers the new account and its funding authorization.
